limitations: Three original interval-selection differences now match: exact weight, width and oblique intervals select one descriptor group instead of loading distinct tied groups.
All six new group checks pass in the native and workerd suites. Composite weight/width/angle and group-before-unicode-range checks also match Chromium in all variants.

Narrow-interval and reversed-interval tie checks differ in every Chromium variant. CSS Fonts 4 permits a user agent to choose one remaining font consistently. Nimbo prefers narrower descriptor intervals; identical descriptor groups retain segmented unicode-range faces.
The four remaining original differences are italic, oblique, isolated surrogate handling and full Unicode case folding. They are not treated as evidence of a browser defect.
The fixture uses an owned static TrueType font; declared variable intervals do not prove variable font decoding, shaping, readiness or rendering.
The inspected upstream WPT sources are references only. The full unmodified upstream test suite has not been executed in Nimbo.
